headline: Red Sox crush the Jays and finally find a rhythm
morning_brew: That is exactly how you handle business at Fenway. After the absolute mess we saw on Friday, seeing the boys bounce back with a dominant 6-1 win over the Blue Jays was just what the doctor ordered. Ranger Suarez was dealing on the mound, keeping Toronto guessing for four scoreless innings before the bullpen took the baton and finished the job. It feels like this team finally found a little rhythm again, and winning the series finale sets a great tone before we pack our bags for the West Coast.

The offense finally showed up when it counted, with Jarren Duran leading the charge by driving in two runs on three singles. And how about Jahmai Jones? A pinch-hit, two-run double that blew the game wide open. That is the kind of bench production we have been screaming for all season. It wasn't perfect, and we still have some questions to answer as the trade deadline looms, but for one night, the team looked like a legitimate contender. My neighbor Rick didn't have a single complaint about the officiating for once, which is frankly more shocking than the win itself. I haven't seen Rick that quiet since he spent three hours trying to explain why the T breakdown was actually a secret government plot.

We are off to California now for a long stretch starting with the Athletics tonight, and we need to keep this momentum rolling. We are sitting at 54-50, and if we can stack a few more wins in this series, we might actually convince ourselves that a postseason push is in the cards. I am not saying anything, I do not want to jinx it, but this team is cooking right now. Let's hope the bats stay warm on the road because these west-coast swings are always a grind.

news_digest.headline: Athletics take on the Red Sox in first of 4-game series
news_digest.dans_take: Time to show the A's why we are fighting for a spot in the AL East.
